mcqs.stem: Best guess: what is the combined self-employment tax rate (before the wage base cap)?

choices.explanation: That's the employee share of FICA.
That's only the Social Security portion.
Correct. SE tax = 12.4% Social Security + 2.9% Medicare.

mcqs.explanation: SE tax = 12.4% Social Security + 2.9% Medicare.

mcqs.stem: A self-employed taxpayer has net profit of $50,000 and no wages. What is the SE tax (rounded)?

choices.explanation: Uses only the Social Security rate.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer has MAGI of $230,000, including $40,000 of net investment income. What is the net investment income tax?
mcqs.explanation: NIIT = 3.8% × lesser of NII (40,000) or excess MAGI (30,000) = **1,140**.

mcqs.stem: Which item is added back in computing AMTI?

choices.text: Qualified residence interest on acquisition debt
choices.explanation: Acquisition-debt interest is allowed for AMT.

choices.text: State income taxes deducted as an itemized deduction
choices.explanation: Correct. Taxes deducted for regular tax aren't allowed for AMT.

choices.text: Municipal interest on general obligation bonds
choices.explanation: Only private activity bond interest is a preference.

mcqs.explanation: Taxes deducted for regular tax aren't allowed for AMT.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises incentive stock options with a $40,000 bargain element and holds the shares. What is the tax effect in the year of exercise?

choices.text: $40,000 of ordinary income for regular tax
choices.explanation: ISOs don't create regular-tax income at exercise.

choices.text: Nothing for regular or AMT purposes
choices.explanation: The spread is an AMT adjustment.

choices.text: $40,000 of capital gain in that year
No regular tax, but a $40,000 AMT adjustment
choices.explanation: Correct. The ISO bargain element is an AMT adjustment at exercise.

mcqs.explanation: The ISO bargain element is an AMT adjustment at exercise.

mcqs.stem: For 2025 the single AMT exemption is $88,100, reduced by 25% of AMTI over $626,350. Single taxpayer, 2025 AMTI of $700,000. What is the AMT exemption after the phase-out?
For 2025 the kiddie-tax threshold is $2,700. A 12-year-old has $5,000 of interest income and no earned income in 2025. How much is taxed at the parents' rate?
mcqs.explanation: Unearned income above $2,700 is taxed at the parents' rate.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer's prior-year AGI was $120,000 and prior-year tax was $18,000. What minimum total of withholding and estimates avoids the underpayment penalty this year (using the prior-year safe harbor)?

choices.explanation: That's 90% of the prior year; the prior-year safe harbor is 100%.
110% applies only if prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000.

mcqs.explanation: Safe harbor: 100% of prior-year tax (110% if prior-year AGI > $150,000).

mcqs.stem: A married couple filing jointly has combined wages of $300,000. How much additional Medicare tax applies?
mcqs.explanation: 0.9% × 50,000 = **450** (employers withhold only on wages over $200,000 per employee; the return reconciles).

mcqs.stem: The 2025 Social Security wage base is $176,100. A taxpayer has $150,000 of wages and $60,000 of net self-employment income in 2025. On what amount of net SE earnings does the 12.4% Social Security portion apply?

choices.explanation: Only up to the remaining wage base.
Wages are below the wage base.
Uses net profit before the 92.35% factor and ignores the cap.

mcqs.explanation: Net SE earnings = 60,000 × 92.35% = 55,410; Social Security applies only to the 26,100 of wage base remaining. Medicare (2.9%) applies to all 55,410.

mcqs.stem: When is the fourth-quarter estimated tax payment for 2025 due for an individual?

choices.explanation: Correct. Individual estimates: April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15 of the following year.
That isn't an estimated tax due date.

mcqs.explanation: Individual estimates: April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15 of the following year.

mcqs.stem: Why does AMT paid because of ISO exercises create a minimum tax credit?

choices.text: Because ISO gains are permanently excluded from income
It's a timing item; the credit prevents double taxation
choices.explanation: Correct. AMT from deferral items (ISOs, depreciation) generates a credit usable in later years; exclusion items (SALT) don't.

choices.text: Because all AMT paid is refundable in later years
Because the credit is required for municipal bond interest
choices.explanation: Private activity bond interest is an exclusion item.

mcqs.explanation: AMT from deferral items (ISOs, depreciation) generates a credit usable in later years; exclusion items (SALT) don't.

mcqs.stem: Net earnings from self-employment are $350. How much SE tax is due?

choices.explanation: Correct. No SE tax is due when net SE earnings are under $400.

mcqs.explanation: No SE tax is due when net SE earnings are under $400.

mcqs.stem: For 2025, a single taxpayer has taxable income of $60,000, including $10,000 of qualified dividends. Use these given 2025 amounts: ordinary rates of 10% up to $11,925, 12% up to $48,475 and 22% up to $103,350; the 0% rate on qualified dividends applies only to taxable income up to $48,350, and 15% applies above that. What is the regular tax?

choices.explanation: This taxes the dividends at ordinary rates.
Correct. Ordinary income of 50,000: 1,192.50 + 4,386 + 22% × 1,525 (335.50) = 5,914. The dividends stack from 50,000 to 60,000, all above 48,350, so 15% × 10,000 = 1,500. Total 7,414.
This taxes the dividends at 0%; they sit above the 0% breakpoint.

mcqs.explanation: Tax ordinary income on the schedule, then stack preferential income on top to find its rate.

mcqs.stem: A sole proprietor has net earnings of $50,000 from self-employment for 2025 and no wages. What is the SE tax?
How does a self-employed individual treat the deductible half of her SE tax?

choices.explanation: Correct. It is an adjustment to income.

choices.text: On Schedule C as an expense

mcqs.explanation: §164(f): half of SE tax is deductible as an adjustment in arriving at AGI.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer's MAGI is $260,000, including $40,000 of net investment income. What is the NIIT?

choices.explanation: Only part of MAGI is taxed.

mcqs.explanation: NIIT = 3.8% × the lesser of NII or MAGI over $200,000 (single).

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer's MAGI is $215,000, including $50,000 of net investment income. What is the NIIT?
mcqs.explanation: NIIT = 3.8% × lesser of NII ($50,000) or excess MAGI ($15,000) = $570.

mcqs.stem: Which item is excluded from net investment income for the NIIT?

choices.explanation: Correct. Qualified plan and IRA distributions are excluded.

mcqs.explanation: NII excludes distributions from qualified plans and IRAs, wages and active trade or business income.

mcqs.stem: An employer pays $230,000 of wages to a single employee in 2025. How much additional Medicare tax must the employer withhold?
mcqs.explanation: Employers withhold the 0.9% additional Medicare tax on wages over $200,000 paid to an employee, regardless of filing status.

mcqs.stem: Prior-year AGI was $200,000 and prior-year tax was $30,000. Current-year tax will be $50,000. What is the minimum timely payment to avoid the estimated-tax penalty?

choices.explanation: The prior-year safe harbor is lower.

mcqs.explanation: The required annual payment is the lesser of 90% of current tax or 100% of prior tax (110% if prior AGI exceeded $150,000).

mcqs.stem: No estimated-tax penalty applies if the tax due after withholding and credits is less than:

choices.explanation: Correct. A de minimis exception applies.

mcqs.explanation: §6654(e)(1): no penalty applies if the tax shown, less withholding, is under $1,000.

mcqs.stem: Which income is taxed at the preferential capital gains rates in the regular tax computation?

choices.explanation: They are taxed at ordinary rates.
They are taxed at ordinary rates.

mcqs.explanation: Qualified dividends are taxed at the same 0%, 15% and 20% rates as net long-term capital gain.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer has $250,000 of net earnings from self-employment (after the 92.35% factor) and no wages. How much additional Medicare tax applies?

choices.explanation: Only the excess over $200,000 is taxed.
The tax applies to SE income too.

mcqs.explanation: The 0.9% additional Medicare tax applies to SE income above $200,000 for single filers.

mcqs.stem: A married couple filing jointly has MAGI of $300,000, including $80,000 of net investment income. What is the NIIT?

choices.explanation: Only part of MAGI is taxed.

mcqs.explanation: NIIT = 3.8% × lesser of NII ($80,000) or MAGI over $250,000 ($50,000).

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer sells her home at a $300,000 gain, excluding $250,000 under §121. Her other income is $210,000 (no other NII). What is the NIIT?

choices.explanation: Use the lesser of NII and excess MAGI.

mcqs.explanation: Only the taxable portion of the home sale gain is NII. MAGI is $260,000; NIIT = 3.8% × lesser of $50,000 or $60,000.

mcqs.stem: When is an individual's second-quarter estimated tax payment for 2025 due?

choices.explanation: Correct. June 15 fell on a Sunday.

mcqs.explanation: Individual estimated payments are due April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15, moved to the next business day when they fall on a weekend.

mcqs.stem: In December, a taxpayer realizes she underpaid estimated tax all year. Which step can best avoid the penalty for earlier quarters?

choices.text: Make a large January estimated payment
choices.explanation: It only covers the last quarter.

choices.text: File the return early in January

choices.explanation: Correct. Withholding is treated as paid evenly.

mcqs.explanation: Withholding is treated as paid ratably through the year unless the taxpayer elects otherwise, so late-year withholding can cure earlier shortfalls.

mcqs.stem: A self-employed author earns most of her 2025 income in December. Which approach can reduce or eliminate penalties for earlier estimated tax installments?

choices.text: Paying it all with the return

choices.explanation: Correct. Installments are based on income earned to date.

choices.text: Filing an extension of time to file

mcqs.explanation: The annualized method matches required installments to when income is earned.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer's 2024 AGI was $160,000 and 2024 tax $20,000. His 2025 tax will be $40,000. What is his prior-year safe harbor amount?

choices.explanation: Correct. 110% applies when prior AGI exceeds $150,000.

mcqs.explanation: Taxpayers with prior-year AGI over $150,000 must pay 110% of prior-year tax for the safe harbor.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer owns a manufacturing business in which he works full time and also has a passive rental. Which income is subject to the NIIT?

choices.explanation: Correct. Active business income isn't NII.

mcqs.explanation: NII includes passive trade or business income and rents, not income from a business in which the taxpayer materially participates.

mcqs.stem: Which item is included in net investment income?
mcqs.explanation: NII includes interest, dividends, capital gains (including fund distributions), rents and nonqualified annuities.

mcqs.stem: A married taxpayer filing separately earns $150,000 of wages. How much additional Medicare tax does she owe?
mcqs.explanation: The additional Medicare tax threshold is $125,000 for married filing separately.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer runs two sole proprietorships: one earns $50,000 and the other loses $20,000. What net earnings are used for SE tax?

choices.explanation: Correct. Combine the businesses, then apply 92.35%.

mcqs.explanation: SE income is figured on the combined net profit of all trades or businesses.

mcqs.stem: A general partner receives a $40,000 guaranteed payment and a $60,000 share of ordinary business income. What are her net earnings from self-employment before the 92.35% factor?

choices.explanation: Correct. Both are SE income for a general partner.

mcqs.explanation: A general partner's SE income includes guaranteed payments for services and the distributive share of ordinary income.

mcqs.stem: A single filer has $40,000 of ordinary taxable income and $20,000 of qualified dividends (total $60,000). The 0% rate applies up to $48,350. How are the dividends taxed?

choices.explanation: Correct. Ordinary income fills the brackets first.

mcqs.explanation: Qualified dividends stack on top of ordinary income for the preferential rate brackets.

mcqs.stem: A 64-year-old who retired this year underpaid estimated tax because of reasonable cause. Can the penalty be waived?

choices.explanation: Correct. Waivers apply to retirees 62+ with reasonable cause.

mcqs.explanation: The IRS may waive the penalty for taxpayers who retired after age 62 or became disabled, if the underpayment was due to reasonable cause.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer has $150,000 of wages and $100,000 of net SE income (after the 92.35% factor). How much additional Medicare tax applies to the SE income?

choices.explanation: The threshold is reduced only by wages.
Correct. The $200,000 threshold is reduced by wages: 0.9% × ($100,000 − $50,000).

mcqs.explanation: For SE income, the threshold is reduced (not below zero) by wages subject to the additional Medicare tax.

mcqs.stem: What is the combined self-employment tax rate on net earnings up to the Social Security wage base?
mcqs.explanation: Self-employment tax is 15.3% up to the wage base and 2.9% above it.

mcqs.stem: What is the net investment income tax rate?
mcqs.explanation: The net investment income tax is 3.8% of the lesser of net investment income or MAGI above the threshold.

mcqs.stem: For a single filer, at what wage level does the 0.9% additional Medicare tax begin?
mcqs.explanation: The additional Medicare tax applies above $200,000 (single), $250,000 (joint) or $125,000 (MFS).

mcqs.stem: A self-employed individual has $100,000 of net SE income and no wages. What is the deduction for half of SE tax (rounded)?

choices.explanation: Uses only the Social Security rate.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer has 2025 modified AGI of $260,000, including $30,000 of net investment income. What is her net investment income tax?

choices.explanation: Correct. 3.8% × the lesser of NII (30,000) or MAGI over $200,000 (60,000).
That applies 3.8% to the 60,000 excess of MAGI over the threshold.
That applies 3.8% to all of MAGI.
0.9% is the additional Medicare tax rate, not the NIIT rate.

mcqs.explanation: NIIT = 3.8% × the lesser of net investment income or MAGI above $200,000 (single): 3.8% × $30,000 = $1,140.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer's 2024 AGI was $180,000 and his 2024 tax was $30,000. His 2025 tax is expected to be $40,000. What is the minimum he must pay through withholding and timely estimates to avoid an underpayment penalty?

choices.explanation: 100% of prior-year tax is enough only if prior-year AGI was $150,000 or less.
90% of current-year tax works but isn't the minimum here.
Correct. Prior-year AGI over $150,000 requires 110% of prior-year tax (33,000), which is less than 90% of current-year tax (36,000).
Paying 100% of current-year tax isn't required.

mcqs.explanation: Safe harbor: the lesser of 90% of current-year tax or 100% of prior-year tax (110% when prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000). Lesser of $36,000 and $33,000 = $33,000.

mcqs.stem: A sole proprietor has 2025 net self-employment income of $50,000 and no wages. What is the self-employment tax?

choices.explanation: That applies only the 12.4% Social Security rate.

mcqs.explanation: SE tax = net earnings × 92.35% × 15.3% (below the wage base); half is deductible for AGI.

mcqs.stem: A single employee earns $260,000 of wages in 2025. What additional Medicare tax applies?
mcqs.explanation: IRC §3101(b)(2): 0.9% of wages above $200,000 (single).

flashcards.back: Net profit × 92.35% × 15.3% (SS portion capped at the wage base); deduct half for AGI.

flashcards.front: Social Security wage base and SE tax
flashcards.back: The 12.4% portion applies only up to the annual wage base, reduced by W-2 Social Security wages; the 2.9% Medicare portion has no cap. (The exam gives the dollar amount.)
3.8% × lesser of NII or MAGI over $200,000 / $250,000.
An exemption by filing status, reduced by 25% of AMTI above a threshold, is subtracted before applying the 26%/28% rates. (The exam gives the dollar amount.)
A child's unearned income above the threshold is taxed at the parents' rate (under 19, or under 24 if a full-time student). (The exam gives the dollar amount.)
